raw_response:
I'm 62 this year, and these 10 mu of land in Quzhou have been my life for 40 years. Finished middle school back when that meant something, but honestly the fields taught me more than any teacher. It's just me now since my wife passed, so I have to be smart about labor — I can't do everything myself anymore, and hiring help costs money I don't always have.

This year I'm sticking with what I know: cotton as my main crop on 6 mu, chili on 2.5 mu, and a small plot of mungbean on 1.6 mu. I'm too old to gamble on new varieties. The extension guy keeps talking about precise fertilizer rates, but I know my soil. I've always put down a bit more nitrogen than they recommend — last year I cut back to try their way and the boll set was thinner. Never again. Loss hurts worse than waste.

For the cotton, I'm planting hybrid seed in late April, about 110 yuan per mu. I'll plow and harrow first, then put base fertilizer in the furrows — compound fertilizer plus some urea. That's one application. Then topdress at flowering in early July, and another light dose when the bolls are filling in August. Seventeen kilograms of nitrogen per mu total, maybe 7 of phosphorus and 5 of potash. I irrigate three times: before planting, at flowering, and at full boll. The pump electricity isn't cheap but you can't skip flowering water. For pests, I'll spray herbicide before planting and insecticide a couple times in summer. I expect about 290 kg of lint per mu if the weather cooperates. I'll need to hire pickers for the main harvest — probably 8 days of hired labor — because my back can't handle bending all day anymore.

The chili is 2.5 mu, planted late April to early May. Chili is labor hell but the price was decent last year. I use an improved hot pepper variety, about 70 yuan per mu for seed. Chili needs more potassium than cotton — I learned that years ago when the peppers were small and pale. So I put down about 10 kg of potassium per mu, plus 15 kg nitrogen and 6 kg phosphorus. Three fertilizer applications: base, then at flowering, then at peak fruit set. I irrigate four times because peppers need steady moisture. I'll need hired women from the village for picking — maybe 10 days total at 80 yuan a day — because chili has to be picked every few days when it turns red.

The mungbean is my quick cash on 1.6 mu, planted in early June after I finish the cotton planting rush. It's only 80 days, harvested by mid-August before the heavy cotton picking starts. I plant an improved local variety, about 35 yuan per mu. Mungbean doesn't need much — the roots fix nitrogen for next year's soil anyway. Just 4 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 2 kg potassium, in two applications. Two irrigations, maybe one insecticide spray. I'll manage most of the mungbean harvest myself with maybe 2 days of help.

Total input cost this year will run me about 4,900 yuan. That's a big chunk of cash for one old man. Seed, fertilizer, pesticide, pump electricity, and hired labor — it all adds up fast. But if cotton stays around 7 yuan per jin and chili prices hold, I should clear enough to get through the year. No room for experiments at my age. Do what works, hope the weather holds, and don't run out of cash before harvest.
